notes: SHIP v1.14.447 - R7: THE CAMERA FRAMES THE RACK. TWO CONSTANTS, AND THEY ARE THE LARGEST VISUAL WIN OF THE PROGRAMME SO FAR. Camera is the one term the RACK SCENE LOCK leaves open, and both changes are backed by the directive AND by the approved mockup rather than by taste. ISO YAW 0.5 rad (28.6 degrees) TO 0.30 rad (17.2 degrees). Section 28 asks for approximately 12 to 20 degrees of yaw and says in as many words not to treat that as a locked constant, and the approved mockup's ISO is rotateY(-17deg). The .255 value of 0.5 predates both documents. 17.2 degrees is the middle of the band and within a fifth of a degree of the mockup. AND R2 IS WHY IT NOW MATTERS, which is the part worth keeping. Deepening the cabinet from RD 4.5 to 9.0 doubled how much side face any given yaw exposes. Projected width is RW times cos-theta plus RD times sin-theta, so at 28.6 degrees the front face measured 5.27 of 9.58 units - only 55 percent, with the black side panel taking the other 45 percent and burying the face where every device and every RU position lives. At 17.2 degrees the front is 5.74 of 8.37, or 69 percent. Section 28's own bound is exactly this: enough yaw to expose cabinet side and depth, not so much that RU positions become hard to read. A good R2 decision made a pre-existing camera value wrong, and only looking at the two together showed it. Elevation is UNTOUCHED at 0.18 - section 28 sets no target for it. FRAME FILL 1.3 TO 1.12. fitDistH is by construction the distance at which the rack's height exactly spans the vertical field of view, so the trailing multiplier IS the breathing room. At 1.3 the rack occupied one over 1.3, or 77 percent of frame height, leaving 23 percent dead air in a preview that R1-D had to fight to get on screen at all. 1.12 gives 89 percent fill with an 11 percent margin - breathing room rather than emptiness - and grows the rack about 16 percent linearly for nothing. Section 27 asks for the rack vertically centred, full cabinet visible, minimal unused space, slight breathing room top and bottom. PERSPECTIVE ONLY, CHECKED NOT ASSUMED. FRONT and REAR are ORTHOGRAPHIC and take their size from ORTHO_MARGIN at 1.08, which is 93 percent fill, not from this distance - so the elevation views do not move at all, and ISO and FRONT now sit at a consistent fill instead of 77 against 93. FOV stays 28. No geometry, material, light, colour or exposure change. VERIFIED ACROSS THE PHONE WIDTHS SECTION 48 ASKS FOR: 360x800 mount 296x320 canvas 592x640, 390x844 mount 326x320 canvas 652x640, 430x932 mount 366x320 canvas 732x640. No horizontal overflow at any width. Visible rack above the fold rises with width - 132, 176 and 264 pixels - and the R1-D floor still holds at every one. RUNS (phone-webkit, each spec ALONE given the 18-hour exhaustion signature recorded at .445): 30 = 4 passed, 29 = 4 passed, 31 = 4 passed, 06-composition = 12 passed, 02-build-forge = 14 passed including the x10 aisle round trip, 08-forge-layout = 17 passed. Tablet and desktop tiers, 06-composition on tablet-webkit plus desktop-chromium = 23 passed, confirming the desktop grid composition is untouched. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 12 style blocks brace-balanced, 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep at .447. DEVICE-VERIFY, one look: open BUILD with an active rack. PASS is a rack that fills the preview with its FRONT face clearly dominant - trays, rails and RU positions readable at a glance - with only a thin margin top and bottom. FAIL is a rack still adrift in empty space, a cabinet whose black side panel is as wide as its face, or any part of the cabinet clipped by the preview edges.
